title: Add incident_type(+subtype) to alert payloads + incident creation API
author: Dylan Brooks
release_notes: Internal: alert payloads and incident creation endpoints now accept incident_type/incident_subtype. Backwards-compatible; missing fields map to "unknown" until producers migrate.
description: Summary: This PR adds `incident_type` and `incident_subtype` fields to our internal alert payload schema (the payload that flows from alerting -> incident ingestion -> incident-bot) and extends the incident creation endpoints to accept and persist those fields. Motivation: As part of the Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping program, we need a structured way to propagate classification signals from alert sources into the incident record so the incident-bot can pre-populate classification and we can report on incident volume by type with minimal manual effort. What changed: (1) `AlertPayload` schema: add optional string fields `incident_type` and `incident_subtype` (intentionally strings for v1 to keep ingestion flexible while taxonomy stabilizes; allowlisted validation will be enforced at the incident-bot / control-plane mapping layer). (2) `POST /internal/incidents` and `POST /internal/incidents/:id/events`: accept `incident_type`/`incident_subtype` and store on incident record + include in read APIs used by ops tooling. (3) Incident ingestion: if payload omits type/subtype, we set `incident_type="unknown"` and `incident_subtype=""` and log a structured warning once per incident to aid migration tracking. (4) Migration: added docs and a temporary dual-write shim for legacy producers so existing alerts continue to open incidents; no producer changes required to merge this PR. (5) Tests: contract tests for alert payload decoding, API request validation, and a regression test ensuring legacy payloads still open incidents and default to `unknown`. Compatibility / rollout plan: This is backwards compatible. Producers can start sending the fields opportunistically; ingestion will not reject unknown values yet. Follow-up work will add an allowlist + owner mapping enforcement in control plane (ENG-4825) and make classification required at close in incident-bot (ENG-4822). Notes: This PR does NOT add metric labels for incident type (separate work with cardinality guardrails in ENG-4826).
commits: api(incidents): accept + persist incident_type fields on create + event ingest
ingest: default missing incident_type to unknown; add migration warning log
tests: contract tests for legacy payloads + incident_type persistence
docs: migration notes for alert producers
review_conversation:
Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure these new fields don't accidentally end up as high-cardinality metric labels downstream? Also, please confirm we’re not validating freeform values at ingest yet—otherwise we'll break producers.
Dylan Brooks (author): Yep—no metrics changes in this PR. Ingest treats as opaque strings and defaults to unknown if missing. Allowlist/validation will happen in incident-bot + owner-mapping config (ENG-4825/4822). I added a comment in the schema README and in the migration doc calling out cardinality risk + where enforcement will live.

Aisha Bello (review): For reporting, do we have a stable place where the incident record stores the final classification (vs. whatever the alert guessed)? I want to avoid dashboards using "suggested" values.
Dylan Brooks (author): Good call. The API stores `incident_type` on the incident record, but it’s mutable. Alert payload values are only used to seed the initial incident fields on create; subsequent edits overwrite. I also added an `incident_type_source` internal field in the model as "alert|manual" so we can filter later if needed (currently not exposed).

Ravi Menon (review): For routing-related alerts, we often know the fallback_reason and could map it to taxonomy. Are we okay with string enums now? I’m worried we'll end up with inconsistent names.
Dylan Brooks (author): For v1, yes—strings with a recommended set in docs. The control-plane mapping config will be the canonical allowlist. Also, routing will soon emit structured fallback_reason enums (separate PR) and we can map that to incident_type consistently at the producer layer.

Devon Price (review): Incident-bot currently expects incident_type to be set by the commander in the modal. With this change, do we pre-populate it? If so, ensure the UI still forces explicit confirmation.
Dylan Brooks (author): This PR only plumbs the field through payload + API. Incident-bot pre-population is in incident-bot PR-812. We’ll keep the confirmation step (dropdown defaulting to whatever is present).

Allison Grant (request changes): Please add a regression test that legacy alert payloads still deserialize and open incidents, and document defaulting behavior.
Dylan Brooks (author): Added `alert_ingest_legacy_payload_opens_incident_defaults_unknown` and updated migration doc with defaulting behavior + log message. Pushed in commit 4/5.
Aisha Bello (approve): Looks good. Thanks for keeping metrics out of this PR and adding the source note.
Allison Grant (approve): Approved after tests + docs updates.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Dylan Brooks. Post-merge note: producers can start sending incident_type immediately; SRE will track adoption via ingest warning logs until incident-bot enforcement lands.
